rules.rationale: Electronegative halide p states sit deep below the Fermi level, giving strongly ionic solids the widest experimental gaps.
Main-group oxides lack partially filled d bands, so conduction edges stay high and measured gaps remain wide.
Polarizable S, Se, Te p states raise the valence-band edge, systematically narrowing gaps relative to oxides and halides.
Low mean atomic number implies compact orbitals, weak spin-orbit splitting, and low polarizability, all widening band gaps.
